# `kernel/execution/DodadGranularEdit.js`

> **Source:** `webgpu-os/kernel/execution/DodadGranularEdit.js`

Revision-bound, authority-neutral Dodad edit preparation. Provider output is decoded into exact text anchors and structural operations, then applied transactionally to an immutable in-memory revision. This module performs no storage or tool dispatch. Callers must run the complete Dodad verifier against `files` before committing the exact admitted changes.

Re-admit one normalized plan against the exact current Artifact graph. Provider plans and durable checkpoint restores share this boundary so a hash-valid plan cannot bypass newer path, source, or entrypoint semantics.

Build a revision-local semantic shortcut map with exact source slices. Lexical facts remain advisory; exact source bytes remain edit authority.

### `buildGranularDodadUpdatePrompt(objective, context, { mutationId = 'dodad-edit:pending', reasonCodes = [], failures = [], repairEvidence = [], structural = false, atomicJson = false, unit = null, checkpoint = null, repairFocus = null, } = {})`

### `selectGranularDodadPromptSourceUnits(context, { unit = null, repairFocus = null, sourceBudget = null, } = {})`

Project the exact source neighborhood shared by staged prompt authoring and adaptive output sizing. Exact identity leads; deterministic lexical, typo, and typed-graph evidence can rank only revision-frozen source units. The ranker cannot widen edit authority or replace exact range validation.

### `async createDodadGranularUpdateEnvelope(input = {}, { expected = null } = {})`

### `parseDodadSearchReplaceBlocks(value, { defaultPath = null } = {})`

Decode canonical raw blocks and Aider-compatible SEARCH/REPLACE blocks. Returned old/new bodies preserve their original line terminators exactly.

### `async parseGranularDodadUpdateEnvelope(value, context, { mutationId = null, defaultPath = null, } = {})`

Parse JSON or raw provider transport and bind authority fields locally.

### `projectGranularDodadDraft(value, { defaultPath = null } = {})`

Project inert replacement bodies for a quarantined live-draft view.

### `createDodadJsonPrefixRecognizer({ fenced = false, onStringStart = null, onStringChunk = null, onStringEnd = null, } = {})`

Incremental JSON grammar recognizer used only to reject an answer-channel transport once it can no longer become one valid JSON object. It visits each received code unit once; incomplete strings, numbers, literals, containers, and an optional closing Markdown fence remain admissible prefixes.

### `createGranularDodadDraftProjector({ defaultPath = null, context = null, checkpoint = null, allowedPaths = null, unitId = null, requireUnitBoundary = false, } = {})`

Incrementally project only inert replacement bodies using Forge preview fields. Exact line projections are derived locally from the immutable input checkpoint; provider-supplied line numbers are never accepted as authority.

### `async applyDodadGranularUpdate(contextInput, envelopeInput)`

Apply every edit and structural operation to the same exact base snapshot. The returned candidate is all-or-nothing and this function mutates no input.

### `async createDodadStagedWorktree(contextInput, { mutationId, planHash = null, admittedPlan = null, objective = '', structuralAllowed = false, resumeCheckpoint = null, maximumIntegrationRepairUnits = null, } = {})`

Create one execution-local copy-on-write staging index. Each unit edits the current staged bytes, so later units may refine earlier staged output. A deterministic local squash derives the final base-relative transaction. Preparing a unit never mutates the stage; only `commitUnit` advances it.

## Notes & Examples

### Command Bus Pattern

The OS uses a capability-gated command bus for inter-app and system communication. Apps register command handlers; the kernel routes commands based on capabilities. Commands can be local (same app), cross-app (with permission), or system-level (elevated).

**Example: Command registration and invocation**
```js
import { CommandBus } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/CommandBus.js';
import { Capability } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/Capability.js';

const bus = new CommandBus();

// Register a handler (requires 'ui' capability)
bus.register('myapp:openFile', async (path) => {
  const content = await storage.read(path);
  return { content, size: content.length };
}, { capability: 'storage' });

// Invoke locally
const result = await bus.invoke('myapp:openFile', '/docs/readme.md');

// Cross-app invocation (requires 'interop' capability)
const otherApp = bus.proxy('otherapp');
const data = await otherApp.invoke('otherapp:compute', input);

// Broadcast to all listening apps
bus.broadcast('system:themeChanged', { theme: 'dark' });
```

**See also:** [WebGPU OS Architecture](/webgpu-os/architecture.md) · [Security Model](/concepts/security-model.md)
